newsitem.title: UK: British government urges action on child abduction.
newsitem.headline: British government urges action on child abduction.

text.p: The British government called on Tuesday for better guidelines and stricter enforcement of orders involving international tug-of-love child abductions.
More than 1,000 children are illegally snatched from Britain each year after their parents divorce or separate.

Despite international conventions aimed at dealing with cross-border abductions, differences in legal systems and lack of enforcement have resulted in lengthy and costly battles for parents and sometimes years of separation from their children.

"The Hague Convention has made a difference but because of public concern we want to take things further," member of parliament Gary Streeter told reporters as the government published a consultation paper on child abduction.

The initiative, launched ahead of a Special Commission of the Hague Conference in March 1997, called for more enforcement of orders, legal aid for parents in all countries participating in the convention and the development of guidelines to get speedier results.
"We would like to do all we can to get the system working effectively...causing the least amount of distress," Streeter added.
More than 40 countries have ratified the Hague Convention on the Civil Aspects of International Child Abduction but many attach different importance to different provisions.

The need for independent professional advice, a speedier appeals procedure, a code of practice for operating the convention and an international panel of arbiters to resolve disputes are among other topics the government hopes to raise at next year's meeting.
